title: BreakdownTasksOutput
description: Output of the breakdown-tasks skill: a list of atomic delegation packets that together fulfill a user request.

summary.description: One-paragraph summary of the overall user request, capturing its goal, scope, and constraints. This gives downstream workers context without requiring them to re-read the full prompt.

tasks.description: An ordered list of atomic delegation packets. Each task should represent a single unit of work that can be completed independently.

dependencies.description: Optional directed dependency map. Keys are task IDs; values are arrays of task IDs that must complete before the key task can begin. Useful for complex multi-stage workflows.

id.description: UUID v4 unique identifier for the task. Used for dependency references, progress tracking, and cross-task traceability.

dependencies.description: List of task IDs (UUID v4) that must complete before this task can begin. Tasks with an empty or absent dependencies array have no prerequisites and may run in parallel.

purpose.description: Single sentence describing what this task accomplishes. Must be actionable and self-contained.

context.description: Expanded context for the worker. Includes the relevant subset of the user prompt, background information, and any constraints. Supports longer prompts up to 8000 characters.

filesToRead.description: Explicit list of file paths the worker must read before starting. No file discovery is permitted beyond this list unless the task packet explicitly authorizes it.

filesToWrite.description: Explicit list of file paths the worker is expected to create or modify. The worker should write every file in this list unless blocked.

skills.description: Skills the worker should load before executing. Each entry must match an available skill name exactly. Loading an unknown skill is a blocker.

executionInstructions.description: Step-by-step instructions for the worker. Each step is a discrete, verifiable action. Steps must be ordered and numbered.

action.description: What to do in this step. Must be concrete and verifiable.

verification.description: Optional: how to verify this step succeeded (e.g., 'File exists at path X', 'Tests pass', 'No error output').
Top-level verification checks the worker must run against their output before finishing. These are checks on the complete deliverable, not per-step checks.

expectedOutput.description: Precise description of the deliverable this task produces. The worker must produce exactly this and nothing more. Use concrete language (file paths, function names, data formats).
